reason: I'll start with filtering blood to see what enters the kidney tube and what stays behind.
expectation: I expect water and other small substances, including glucose and waste, to pass through while blood cells and large proteins stay in the vessels.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would start the route to the bladder, but I want to follow filtering first.

effect: Filtering let useful glucose through along with waste, so the next step is to follow recovery.
reaction: It's interesting that the filter doesn't just remove waste.
reason: The recovery tube is the next part of the filtering goal, and its picture shows useful substances returning to blood.
expectation: I expect glucose, some salts and much of the water to return to blood, leaving some fluid and waste to continue onward.

alternatives.reason: The ureters would build the urine route, but I want to finish following the filtered fluid first.

effect: The kidney recovered useful substances and much water, leaving urine to follow its collecting route. I can now build the route to the bladder.
reaction: It makes sense that the filter takes useful things through too, and the tube takes them back.
reason: The ureters connect the kidneys toward the bladder, so I'll build the route in that order.
expectation: I expect the two ureters to attach to the kidneys, with the bladder still to be added.

alternatives.reason: I could add the bladder first, but following the route from the kidneys seems clearer.

effect: The ureters now connect the kidney outlets toward the bladder position, leaving the bladder to add.
reaction: The squeezing arrows help explain how urine moves along the tubes.
reason: Adding the bladder is the only available combination and completes the route from the kidneys.
expectation: I expect the bladder to attach to both ureters and collect urine.

effect: The bladder completes the route from both kidneys, and the chapter's goals are complete.
reaction: Seeing the same fluid follow the whole route made the connection clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following filtered fluid into the recovery tube was most worthwhile: it showed why the kidney takes useful substances and water back instead of just filtering out waste.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the bladder was straightforward and the only available combination, so it felt less like a decision, even though it completed the model.

surprise.text: The filter lets useful glucose through along with waste; the recovery tube then takes useful substances back.

arbitrary.text: None felt arbitrary: the pictures and goals explained the filter, recovery tube and urine route. The compatible menu still supplied the pairings.

continue.text: Yes, I would try another chapter: following the kidney's filter-and-recovery process was interesting, and the route to the bladder made the result concrete.
